MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  APRIL 22, 2024

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A special meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:02 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council
  Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR
  MCCORMICK.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR MCCORMICK led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Ciarolla, Holdsworth,  Persichina,  and
  McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  Pope, Johnson, and Bain

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH
  19, 2024

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  HOLDSWORTH to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MARCH 19, 2024.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  NEW PROGRAM PROPOSAL – CAMP HAVE-A-BLAST SUMMER CAMP

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
April 22, 2024
   Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the new program proposal for Camp
  Have-A-Blast summer camp (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH asked if there was a way to define the area at
  the park that would be used by the summer camp program to the public who may
  be utilizing the surrounding areas of the park. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff
  would work with the contractor to create a boundary with possible delineators or
  some other method to define the area of the park to the public for the summer
  camp program while it is in session.

  Dylan George, owner of Battle Party LA, gave a brief overview of how they typically
  set-up and run their programs when they have utilized the park previously for
  birthday party park permit rentals.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA asked what the expected age range for the summer
  camp program would be. Mr. George stated that he anticipates ages 7-10 years
  old based on the age range that typically books their activities offered through
  Battle Party LA. Robert Buckley, Chief Operations Officer of GameTruck LA, stated
  that he anticipates ages 10-12 years old based on the typical age range that books
  their activities offered through GameTruck LA.

  CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if this was a new venture between Battle Party LA
  and GameTruck LA or a program that has been offered prior. Mr. Buckley noted
  that this would be a new venture between the two companies and that this would
  be the first time offering this type of program.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that there were no conflicts with any other programming
  or activities offered by the City during the proposed weeks for the summer camp
  program, in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked if accommodations would be available for
  special needs children with the summer camp program. Mr. George stated that
  there could be modifications made to the activities offered at the summer camp to
  accommodate the needs of the child and for them to feel as involved as the other
  children at the camp.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that Staff does recommend that the instructors of City
  contracted programs have CPR/First Aid training prior to the start of the program,
  in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the program instructors would be background
  checked by Livescan. Mr. George noted that while they do background checks for
  all their staff, they do not do it with Livescan. He also noted that they are open to
  utilizing Livescan for their background checks if required.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
April 22, 2024
   CHAIR MCCORMICK asked for a roll call vote to approve the recommendation by
  Staff to offer Camp Have-A-Blast as a new City contracted program.

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Holdsworth, Persichina, and McCormick
  ABSENT:  Pope, Johnson, and Bain

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  SECURITY CAMERA PROJECT UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief update on the security camera project. She noted
  that the project was discussed at the City Council Policy Development Session.
  She reported that City Council has directed Staff to create a Security Camera
  Implementation Plan, obtain cost estimates, and allocate funds in future City
  budgets.

  B.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief update on the upcoming Mayor’s Ride scheduled
  for Saturday, May 11. He reported on the schedule of events for the Mayor’s Ride,
  including the Scout Pancake Breakfast from 7:00 am-11:00 am at Ernie Howlett
  Park. He also provided information regarding how to purchase breakfast tickets for
  the Scout Pancake Breakfast.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA reported that there was a broken picnic table right
  behind Field A at Ernie Howlett Park. He also reported that the missing section of
  fence on the Field B batting cage had still not been repaired. Supervisor Pinuelas
  responded that she would follow up with Silver Spur Little League regarding the
  missing section of fencing.

  CHAIR MCCORMICK reported that there was some minor flooding along the trails
  at the George F Canyon Nature Preserve. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that
  maintenance staff would go and investigate those areas.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
April 22, 2024
   COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH reported issues with some of the fencing at
  Rockbluff Park.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 12, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  FOUNDERS PARK UPDATE

  NONE.

  B.  PICKLEBALL UPDATE

  NONE.

  C.  ASSESSMENT OF SPACE FOR POTENTIAL DOG PARK AND FUTURE PARKS

  NONE.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  CHANDLER PARK, PEPPERWOOD PARK, ROCKBLUFF PARK, AND SILVER
  SPUR PARK

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave an overview of the maintenance of the gopher
  control at Chandler Park. He reported that the City has contracted with a new
  vendor and has seen good progress. He also noted the replacement and
  maintenance of some of the fencing around the park. He stated that the pepper
  trees throughout the City, including the ones in Chandler Park, appear to be dying
  but that it is due to excess moisture affecting the roots of the trees. He stated that
  since the weather has become drier, there appears to be some new growth
  accumulating on some of the trees.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WALKED TO PEPPERWOOD PARK FOR
  A TOUR**

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
April 22, 2024
   Supervisor Pinuelas reported that Staff felt that Pepperwood Park may be a good
  location as a potential space for the installation of a dog run. She noted that these
  are preliminary thoughts and more detailed specifics will be reported once the
  initial assessment of space for a potential dog park/run is done.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WENT TO ROCKBLUFF PARK FOR A
  TOUR**

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH noted the erosion of the trail along the side of
  the slope at Rockbluff Park has begun to seep through the fencing and go into the
  park. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he was aware of the erosion
  accumulating in the specific area and will begin the repairs once the rainy season
  ends.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION DECIDED TO NOT TOUR SILVER SPUR
  PARK**

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR MCCORMICK ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 6:52 PM TO THE NEXT
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON MAY 21, 2024, AT 6:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Matt Morrow  Ryan McCormick
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
April 22, 2024
